items.note: A session event for this mount, listed so the bead's height above the substrate can be computed against it: the reference for the bead-height hand-over statement. Not stated: which drive reported it (the stand's focus drive, presumably, as read in NIS or Micro-Manager), which objective was in place, how the surface was judged in focus, or whether PFS was engaged. A focus-drive difference is not a height in the sample: through oil into water the axial scale differs, and that correction is not applied here.

items.note: Not stated: why the other three do not (trapping needs a high-NA objective, but that reason is not the person's statement and is not recorded as theirs), which of 40x WI and any other 40x is meant (the store's 40x is the water-immersion MRD77400), or whether a trap was ever tried at 20x. For limits: position limits are wanted only for these three objectives, and a missing row means software refuses every trap command at any other objective.

items.fact: On 2026-09-25 at the 100x objective, a trap commanded over TCP to x = +6 um was reported by the person at x = 2 um, y = 0 -- if that is where it appeared, the GUI's um are about a third of physical um at 100x as it was calibrated that day.
items.how: run-20260925-008 sent TRAP_POSITION trap_2 6.0 0.0 (accepted 0). At the hold the person answered 'nope second trap is x = 2um , y = 0.' Whether that reports where the trap appeared, or asks for 2 um, has been asked and not yet answered; no frame of the two traps was analysed.
items.note: Unmeasured until the person says which it was and a frame shows both trap positions against the store's pixel size. If the scale is off, the remedy is the person re-calibrating in the GUI; nothing in code rescales. Until the person states the calibration for the objective in place, the trap-step exemption refuses every position command.

items.fact: Of the 2026-09-25 final recording (trap_2 set by hand at 2.5 um, 1/0.5), which shows no bead and a field about a quarter as bright as before, the person said: "I think we just lost a particle".
